Q: Do TOCTOU vulnerabilities exist in file *existence* checks with access()? A:

The access system call was never designed as a substitute of the actual open. It is used to allow a setuid program to know the permissions the real user id has on the file.

but if you plan to open the file and act upon it, then you need to seteuid first to the real user and open (or fopen) it being the real user id. This will impede an attacker to substitute the file between the two system calls. And you will be able to deal with the race condition you are having properly. The switch between the real and effective uid is possible in unix through the kernel implemented saved uid. No security break if you do things ok. The check of the permissions is also done by the system in the open system call. But never open a file with the wrong credentials or you will damage your system security.

Setuid programs can be a system security breach if you program them wrongly. Nobody tells you to open a user file with the wrong credentials, nor says that you should open the file with the setuid user credentials. But you can switch between both uids to do things properly.

You do this continuously with the login, sudo, su, and passwd commands. And nobody claims a security bug because of this.

The mail command is an splendid example of this kind of thing. It must run as a mail user to have control of the mail directories and the mailboxes of the users, but must check if you have access to the files before acting upon them. You don't allow the mail user id to access your files, but you give (implicitly) access it to your mails (because it must read them to transfer to the remote user, or write them to allow you to receive email) The common use of access here is to check if you have proper credentials on a file that is not yours, but you should have read access to it. The mail command (setuid mail but run by you) should be capable of switching between mail and you to access your files and manage email. It can use access to avoid this exchange if you are just trying to read another user's emails. But finally, when it is time to read your file, it will have to do with real user id (the real user id is the user running a setuid program, in this case a setuid-mail program)

Q: How to measure structural similarity between programs written in different languages A:

What is "structural similarity"? Do you have a formal definition? You can't measure something you can't define. Nevertheless, I'd think the first step would be to bring both programs to common representation, such as LLVM-IR or bitcode, which is luckily can be done for both C and Rust. However this transformation might affect the "similarity" by itself depending on the definition.

Q: How would you describe the Java programming language to a beginner? A:

We cannot really say much since we have no idea what your professors are teaching you. But on your third semester you should have at least learned the basics of the language. And Java is not the most complex of languages, so learning should be relatively easy, as long as you are taught in the right way. When I first started learning Java I worked through The Java™ Tutorials, which allows you to learn at your own pace from the very beginning.
